neighbours.label: letter pieces inside strings that are not ordinary words (spaced-out cipher letters, transliterated native place names)
fire: The puzzle's answer, written backwards, was r e t a w e h t n i.
Their old camp was known as Tsawatenok, which roughly means 'river bend'.
Each line of the code book read like x q r l ! m u p ! z a.
Elders still remember the settlement of Kikawahkotu near the creek.
The intercepted note said only h t r o n o g, which nobody could read.
On the old map the hill is labelled Wichekaxtupa in the native spelling.
Decode this: g n i n r o m d o o g, then send it back.
The spring is called Pitahawiratu in the Skidi dialect.
quiet: The puzzle's answer, written plainly, was in the water.
Their old camp was known as River Bend, which describes its shape.
Each line of the code book read like a short sentence.
Elders still remember the settlement of Pine Hollow near the creek.
The intercepted note said only go north, which everyone could read.
On the old map the hill is labelled Eagle Ridge in English.
Decode this message, then send it back to me.
The spring is called Cold Water in the local dialect.
